static_traits.name: Chen Tao
static_traits.social_status: Has a group of supportive friends, but he feels they do not fully understand his distress about city life
static_traits.medical_history: Not yet had a history of similar psychological problems; not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fair logic; high cooperativeness, positive attitude; emotions dominated by frustration and despair; tendencies toward catastrophizing and all-or-nothing thinking

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling trapped due to living in a city, believing they can never move to the suburbs, continuously producing frustration and despair, affecting academics, relationships, and daily motivation.
basic_info.core_demands: 'These frustrations affected my overall well-being and motivation, prompting me to seek counseling.'; 'I need some guidance on how to move forward.'
growth_experiences: Moved to the city for university, originally thinking it was only temporary; over time, feeling increasingly trapped and helpless, believing the lack of opportunities and financial means makes moving to the suburbs impossible; the trapped feeling intensifies when seeing friends plan to move elsewhere; although having supportive friends, feeling they cannot fully understand these feelings.

core_beliefs: I am unable to change my situation
The future is unfavorable to me, realizing my wish (moving to the suburbs) is impossible

special_situations.event: Seeing friends plan to move to different areas or more ideal residences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot move away like my friends, it means I have failed, will be left behind, and will stay trapped here
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently expressing dissatisfaction with the city to friends to vent emotions, while reducing investment in actual moving plans
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, I will stay trapped here

special_situations.event: Paying attention to moving costs and current insufficient income (e.g. checking rental prices, budgets)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not have enough money now, I can never move to the suburbs
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not making concrete action plans, falling into repeated worry and avoidance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I simply cannot afford to move

special_situations.event: Commuting or daily life in a noisy, crowded urban environment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only living in the suburbs counts as living a better life; in the city one is doomed to suffer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Idealizes suburban life, ignoring any positives or feasible options in the current environment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never be happy here

special_situations.event: Reminded of or thinking of needing to take concrete steps (such as searching for housing, making a savings plan)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try and fail, it proves my incompetence and deepens despair, so it is better not to try lightly
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinates and avoids action to reduce the risk of failure and disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Doing it is useless, I have no control over my situation

core_conflict.wish: Longing for freedom and the right to choose for oneself (being able to move to a quieter suburban life)
core_conflict.fear: Fears trying and failing, being rejected by reality and continuing to be trapped, losing a sense of control
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of failure and disappointment by emphasizing objective obstacles and not taking action
Maintaining the status quo to feel safe

object_relations.object_representation: The city/environment is a force of restriction and rejection
Friends are bystanders who cannot understand

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes concrete action suggestions or asks about feasibility plans (such as researching housing options, making a savings plan)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feels the other person is pushing her to face possible failure; believes external obstacles determine everything and she can hardly control anything herself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, rational tone, emphasizes economic and opportunity constraints, weakens emotional expression, and raises many 'realistic reasons' to postpone action.

manifestations: Long feeling trapped by city life, unable to choose where to live
Predicting they can never move to the suburbs
Views suburban life as the only path to a 'better life'
outcomes: Tense relationships with friends, worsening social experience

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behavioral impulses originally directed outward, turning energy inward instead, often manifesting as self-repression, rumination, or self-harm.
manifestations: Long ruminating on the thought of 'being unable to move' without taking outward action
Turning dissatisfaction with the city into self-stagnation (not gathering information or trying)

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Treating 'must have enough money to move' as an unshakable absolute rule
Treating 'a better life is impossible in the city' as an iron rule, ignoring possible middle options

positive_force: Has a supportive circle of friends (potential for emotional and informational support)
Has clear housing goals and preferences (relocating to the suburbs)
Currently pursuing a nursing degree, possessing a foundation of long-term planning and self-discipline
Can proactively seek help and counseling; willing to try small-step actions
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization are significant
Excessive rumination and avoidance of action maintain stagnation
Low self-efficacy, tending toward external attribution (believing 'everything is against me')
Comparing with others leads to inferiority and despair (comparing and despairing)

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated rumination around 'being unable to move to the suburbs' and persistent despair
antecedent: Seeing friends plan to move or discuss housing choices
When checking rent, budget, and other financial information
When commuting or living in a noisy, crowded urban environment
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and future-predicting cognitions lead to low self-efficacy, believing they cannot change their situation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and the pressure to act, relieving anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Academic performance impaired, interpersonal tension, declining daily motivation and sense of enjoyment

target_behavior.behavior: Avoidance and inaction (not gathering information, planning budgets, or visiting in person)
antecedent: When thinking about needing to make concrete moving steps or facing practical operations
When reminded or feeling they should take action
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing failure and rejection by reality, using rationalization of external obstacles to lower anxiety
target_behavior.function: Immediately reducing the sense of risk of failure and disappointment, maintaining psychological safety
target_behavior.consequence: Problems maintained and stagnating, deepening despair, continuously declining quality of life
